rules.rationale: Acyclic solutes reorient freely, keeping polar groups solvent-exposed and lowering hydration free energy.
Rigid polycyclic scaffolds form poor aqueous cavities and bury polar functionality from water.
Extended aromatic surfaces are hydrophobic and solvophobically penalized, weakening net aqueous affinity.
Branching buries heteroatom sites, cutting solvent-accessible donor and acceptor area.

skills.hypothesis: Ring-free, unbranched, low-aromatic solutes hydrate better because polar groups stay exposed; this may fail for polar heterocycles where ring nitrogens or oxygens hydrogen-bond strongly.

rules.rationale: Dense heteroatoms give strong hydrogen-bond and dipole contacts that stabilize the aqueous phase.
Pure hydrocarbon character lacks polar contacts, so hydration is enthalpically and entropically disfavored.
Short SMILES mark small solutes whose polar groups remain fully solvent-accessible to water.
Longer scaffolds add hydrophobic surface and conformational cost that weaken net hydration.

skills.hypothesis: Heteroatom density and compactness drive hydration free energy through polarity and hydrogen bonding; it may fail when intramolecular hydrogen bonds shield polar groups from solvent.

lesson: The shape-based ring skill again beat the heteroatom prior (63.2 vs 58.1 mean development AUC), but both dropped sharply from the earlier generation, and per-seed spread stayed wide, so keep the shape mechanism deployed with only moderate confidence and unchanged mass settings.
revision_summary: Retained the ring/flexibility skill as deployed after it repeated its development-AUC advantage, kept the aromatic and branching burial penalties, and kept the heteroatom polarity prior as the alternative at lower confidence.
